question2.explanation: Check divisibility in the most specific order. Multiples of both 3 and 5 must be handled before checking either divisor alone.
question2.hint: Print based on divisibility by 3 and 5.

question2.name: Number of Steps to Reduce a Number to Zero

question2.explanation: Repeat the required operation until the number reaches zero. Even values are halved; odd values are decreased by one.
question2.hint: Even: divide by 2. Odd: subtract 1.

question2.name: Subtract the Product and Sum of Digits

question2.explanation: Extract every decimal digit with modulo 10. Add it to the sum, multiply it into the product, and remove it with integer division.
question2.hint: Use % 10 and / 10.

question2.explanation: Reverse the digits using a wider integer type, then compare the reversed value with the original number. Negative numbers cannot be palindromes.
question2.hint: Reverse the digits or compare from both ends.

question2.explanation: A positive power of two has exactly one set bit. Clearing the lowest set bit therefore produces zero.
question2.hint: Keep dividing by 2 while the number is even.

question2.explanation: The permutation values are valid indices. Build each output value directly as nums[nums[i]].
question2.hint: For each i, answer[i] = nums[nums[i]].

question2.explanation: Turn the input into prefix sums. Each position accumulates the total stored immediately before it.
question2.hint: Add the previous running total.

question2.name: Find Numbers with Even Number of Digits

question2.explanation: Count the decimal digits in each number and increment the answer when that count is even.
question2.hint: Count digits for every value.

question2.explanation: Calculate the sum of every customer row and keep the largest row total.
question2.hint: Sum each row and keep the maximum.

question2.explanation: Maintain the current run of ones and the best run seen. Reset the current run whenever a zero appears.
question2.hint: Reset the current count when you see 0.

question2.explanation: The gain array describes changes rather than absolute heights. Accumulate those changes from altitude zero and track the maximum prefix sum.
question2.hint: Track current altitude and maximum altitude.

question2.explanation: Use a write pointer. Copy only values different from val into the front of the same array; the write pointer becomes the new length.
question2.hint: Write only values that are not equal to val.

question2.explanation: Because the array is sorted, duplicates are adjacent. A write pointer advances only when the read value differs from the last unique value.
question2.hint: One pointer reads; one writes unique values.

question2.explanation: Move every non-zero value to the next write position, then fill the remaining suffix with zeroes. Relative order is preserved.
question2.hint: Move non-zero values forward, then fill zeroes.

question2.explanation: Merge from the back so unprocessed values in nums1 are never overwritten. Place the larger current value into the last free position.
question2.hint: Fill nums1 from the end.

question2.explanation: XOR every valid index and every array value. Equal values cancel, leaving only the missing number.
question2.hint: Compare expected and actual sums, or use XOR.

question2.explanation: XOR cancels paired values because x XOR x is zero. The only unpaired number remains.
question2.hint: x XOR x is 0.

question2.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

question2.explanation: Scan once while tracking the lowest price seen before today. The best profit is the largest difference between today’s price and that minimum.
question2.hint: Keep the lowest price seen so far.

question2.explanation: Normalize k, reverse the full array, then reverse the first k values and the remaining values. This places the rotated suffix and prefix correctly.
question2.hint: Reverse all, then reverse the two parts.

question2.explanation: First store the product of all elements to the left. Then walk backward, multiplying each result by the product of elements to the right.
question2.hint: Multiply prefix and suffix products without division.

question2.explanation: Use pointers at both ends and swap their characters while moving toward the center.
question2.hint: Swap characters from both ends.

question2.explanation: Move two pointers inward. Skip non-alphanumeric characters and compare lowercase forms of the remaining characters.
question2.hint: Skip non-alphanumeric characters.

question2.name: First Unique Character in a String

question2.explanation: Count each lowercase letter, then scan the string again. The first character with frequency one is the answer.
question2.hint: Count first, then scan for frequency 1.

question2.explanation: Start with the first word as the candidate prefix. Shorten it until every other word begins with it.
question2.hint: Shrink the candidate prefix until every word matches.

question2.explanation: Anagrams contain identical character frequencies. Increment counts for the first string and decrement them for the second.
question2.hint: Compare character frequencies.

question2.explanation: Insert values into a hash set. If insertion fails, that value was already present.
question2.hint: A repeated insertion reveals a duplicate.

question2.explanation: Store the latest index of every value. A duplicate is valid when the distance from its stored index is at most k.
question2.hint: Store each value’s most recent index.

question2.explanation: For each value, check whether its complement was seen earlier. Store the current value only after the check so one index is never reused.
question2.hint: Look for target - current before storing current.

question2.explanation: Boyer-Moore voting cancels different values in pairs. Since the majority appears more than half the time, it remains as the final candidate.
question2.hint: Start with a map; later learn Boyer-Moore.

question2.explanation: Store the first array in a set and insert matching values from the second array into a result set to remove duplicates.
question2.hint: Store one array in a set and test the other.

question2.explanation: Repeatedly replace the number with the sum of its squared digits. A set detects a cycle; reaching one means the number is happy.
question2.hint: Use a set to detect a repeated sum.

question2.explanation: Sorted letters form the same key for every anagram. Group original strings in a hash map under that canonical key.
question2.hint: Use a sorted word or frequency vector as the key.

question2.explanation: The largest square comes from the value with the largest absolute magnitude at either end. Fill the result backward while moving that pointer.
question2.hint: Compare absolute values at both ends.

question2.name: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

question2.explanation: Because the array is sorted, compare the end values. Move left rightward when the sum is too small and right leftward when it is too large.
question2.hint: Move left or right based on the sum.

question2.explanation: Area is limited by the shorter line. After evaluating a pair, move the shorter side because keeping it cannot produce a better area.
question2.hint: Move the pointer at the shorter line.

question2.explanation: Sort the array, fix one value, and solve a two-pointer two-sum on the remaining suffix. Skip repeated values to avoid duplicate triplets.
question2.hint: Sort, fix one number, then solve two-sum.

question2.explanation: Push opening brackets. For each closing bracket, the stack top must contain its matching opening bracket.
question2.hint: Push opening brackets; match every closing bracket.

question2.explanation: Keep valid round scores on a stack-like vector. Each operation reads or changes only the most recent scores.
question2.hint: Keep valid scores on a stack.

question2.explanation: Process nums2 with a decreasing monotonic stack. When a larger value appears, it becomes the next greater value for every smaller stack top.
question2.hint: Pop smaller values when a greater value appears.

question2.explanation: Store each value together with the minimum at the moment it is pushed. The top pair then answers both top and getMin in constant time.
question2.hint: Store the minimum with each pushed value.

question2.explanation: Maintain a decreasing stack of price-span pairs. Pop all prices no greater than today’s price and add their accumulated spans.
question2.hint: Store price with its accumulated span.

question2.explanation: Compute the first window sum, then slide by adding the entering value and subtracting the leaving value. Track the best sum.
question2.hint: Update the window sum in O(1).

question2.name: Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring

question2.explanation: Count vowels in the first fixed-length window. Slide it by adding the entering character and removing the leaving character.
question2.hint: Add the entering character and remove the leaving one.

question2.explanation: Track each character’s most recent index. If it lies inside the current window, move the left boundary just past that occurrence.
question2.hint: Move left past the previous duplicate.

question2.explanation: Expand the window until its sum reaches the target, then repeatedly shrink from the left while recording the shortest valid length.
question2.hint: Shrink while the sum is large enough.

question2.explanation: Maintain an inclusive search interval. Compare the middle value with the target and discard the half that cannot contain it.
question2.hint: Maintain inclusive low and high boundaries.

question2.explanation: Find the first index whose value is not less than the target. Use a half-open interval so low is the insertion position when the loop ends.
question2.hint: Return the first position where target can go.

question2.explanation: Binary-search for the first version where isBadVersion is true. Keeping high at mid preserves a possible first bad version.
question2.hint: Find the first true value.

question2.explanation: Binary-search for the largest integer whose square does not exceed x. Divide x by mid to avoid multiplication overflow.
question2.hint: Search for the greatest square not exceeding x.

question2.name: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array

question2.explanation: Run lower-bound searches twice: once for target and once for target + 1. Their positions give the first index and one past the last index.
question2.hint: Run separate searches for left and right boundaries.

question2.name: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

question2.explanation: Compare the middle value with the right endpoint. If it is greater, the minimum lies to the right; otherwise the middle may be the minimum.
question2.hint: Compare mid with the right endpoint.

question2.explanation: At least one half is sorted. Determine which half is sorted and whether the target lies inside it, then discard the other half.
question2.hint: Identify the sorted half each step.

question2.explanation: Binary-search the eating speed. A speed is feasible when the sum of ceiling divisions for all piles is no greater than h.
question2.hint: Search the minimum feasible eating speed.

question2.explanation: Iteratively keep the previous two Fibonacci values. Each step shifts the pair forward, avoiding exponential recursive repetition.
question2.hint: Write the base cases first; then optimize.

question2.explanation: Repeatedly divide by three while the division is exact. The original number is a power of three precisely when the final value is one.
question2.hint: Stop at 1 or when division is not exact.

question2.explanation: Use exponentiation by squaring. Recursively calculate the half power once, square it, and multiply by x only for an odd exponent.
question2.hint: Square the half-power; handle odd n once.

question2.explanation: Move slow by one node and fast by two nodes. When fast reaches the end, slow has reached the middle.
question2.hint: Fast moves twice for every slow step.

question2.explanation: Walk through the list while redirecting each next pointer to the previous node. Save the original next node before changing the link.
question2.hint: Track previous, current, and next.

question2.explanation: Use a dummy head and repeatedly append the smaller current node. Attach the remaining non-empty list after one side ends.
question2.hint: Use a dummy head and append the smaller node.

question2.explanation: Move one pointer by one step and another by two. They must eventually meet inside a cycle; without a cycle the fast pointer reaches null.
question2.hint: A cycle makes the pointers meet.

question2.name: Remove Nth Node From End of List

question2.explanation: Start both pointers at a dummy node. Advance fast n + 1 steps, then move both until fast reaches null; slow is just before the node to remove.
question2.hint: Keep a gap of n nodes.

question2.explanation: The depth of an empty tree is zero. Otherwise it is one plus the greater depth of the left and right subtrees.
question2.hint: Depth is 1 + max(left, right).

question2.explanation: Two trees are equal when their current values match and both corresponding left and right subtrees are also equal.
question2.hint: Compare values and both subtrees.

question2.explanation: At every node, recursively invert both subtrees and swap their returned roots.
question2.hint: Swap left and right at every node.

question2.explanation: Simulate recursive inorder traversal with a stack: descend left, visit the node, then continue into its right subtree.
question2.hint: Visit left, node, then right.

question2.explanation: Use breadth-first search. Record the queue size before processing each level so exactly that level’s nodes are grouped together.
question2.hint: Process one queue level at a time.

question2.explanation: Carry an exclusive lower and upper bound down the tree. Every node must lie strictly inside its bounds, which become tighter for its children.
question2.hint: Carry valid lower and upper limits.
